We are seeking a Head of Character Effects (CFX) to support our upcoming animated feature film. The Head of Character Effects works inside of NAS as the show-based leader for all character-related secondary motion, including hair, fur, feathers, cloth, and garments. They will partner closely with the Director, Production Designer, VFX Supervisor, Art Director, Head of Characters, Head of Character Animation and Technical Supervisor to ensure that character effects are both artistically compelling and technically robust.

The Head of Character Effects will oversee the CFX team during asset development, look development, and shot production. They will define the simulation approach for the show, review and give notes on all CFX work, and ensure it meets the highest quality bar while remaining efficient and stable in production. This may involve developing or supervising prototypes, guiding grooming and garment construction for simulation, solving complex technical problems, and helping to set up the CFX side of the project for success.

This position is essential in bridging the gap between creative intent and simulation-driven workflows, ensuring that character motion feels alive, expressive, and fully aligned with the film’s visual language. The Head of Character Effects builds strong relationships with creative leadership and with technical and production partners, demonstrating great diplomatic and interpersonal skills to balance artistic ambition with schedule and pipeline constraints.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and supervise Character Effects across the show, from look development to final shot delivery

  • Define the creative and technical approach for hair, fur, cloth, feathers, and other character-related simulations

  • Review CFX assets and shots, providing clear, actionable artistic and technical notes

  • Collaborate with Directors, Production Designers, Art Directors, Head of Characters, Animation, FX, and Look Development to ensure CFX supports character performance and story

  • Partner with Technical Supervisors, Production Technology, and R&D to develop and maintain robust, efficient CFX tools and workflows

  • Anticipate and identify creative and technical challenges in CFX and offer practical, innovative solutions

  • Work with Production Management on bids, schedules, and priorities to deliver high-quality work on time and within scope

  • Mentor and support CFX Supervisors, Leads, and Artists, fostering growth, clarity, and a positive team culture

  • Collaborate with grace, humility, inclusion, and open-mindedness

info.title: Business Security Partner (L5), Consumer & Content
info.jobDescription:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Team

Netflix’s Business Security Partner (BSP) team is a team of senior security advisors organized around business proximity rather than technical domains. Each BSP partner owns relationships with a defined portfolio of business units, builds long-term relationships with BU leadership, and serves as the security export who understands those businesses well enough to advise on decisions before they are made. We sit in business reviews, participate in architecture conversations, and build the kind of trust with stakeholders that makes security a resource rather than a requirement. 

Across all of our relationships, the goal is the same: every major business decision at Netflix should have access to clear, usable security risk context; not a compliance output buried in a document, but actionable guidance from a partner who understands both the risk and the business. 

About the Role

This role covers two distinct and fast-moving areas within Netflix.  BSP aligns coverage based on need; BSPs also often rotate business units on occasion. You may cover other areas during your time at Netflix.

On the Customer Service side, you will be the primary security partner for a global support organization that is deploying AI capabilities across its consumer-facing operations. You will advise on the security risk of new technologies as they launch, help the organization assess and manage risk for systems that handle significant consumer data volumes, and maintain the overall security posture for a high-scale, globally operating support environment 

For Content Generation, you will partner with teams that are building the next generation of GenAI / GenMedia production pipelines; prosperity models, open-source tools, and third-party inference providers running on CPU compute infrastructure to generate visual context for Netflix productions. Your work will span third-party AI tool evaluations, compute infrastructure security, training data governance, and security control decisions for AI-assisted content workflows. You will partner with multiple cross-functional teams to drive remediation of identified risks. The content these systems touch is pre-release Netflix IP, and the pace of change is high.

This role also carries M&A responsibilities. BSPs at Netflix are expected to support technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 

What You Will Work On:

  • Own the security partnership for Customer Service and Creative Technology, building stakeholder relationships, learning how these businesses operate, and translating that context into opinionated security guidance.

  • Lead security risk assessments and treatment strategies with cross-functional teams as they launch new capabilities and tools.

  • Evaluate and advise on the security posture of GenAI/GenMedia - third-party tool evaluations, open-source model assessments, compute infrastructure security, and training data governance.

  • Maintain and evolve the Business Risk Profile for each business unit, prioritizing and driving remediation of the risks that matter most.

  • Support M&A technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 

  • Develop reporting and metrics that communicate risk posture and business security initiatives to SPA leadership and business unit stakeholders.

Desired Background:

  • Experience with securing GenAI systems, customer-facing deployments, and/or content generation / ML pipelines. You understand what makes AI systems distinct from traditional software.

  • Broad security domain knowledge across application security, cloud security, identity and access management, and data governance. You are comfortable operating across all of them and know when to go deep versus when to synthesize. 

  • Strong stakeholder partnership instincts. You build trust with the business by demonstrating that you understand their context, not just their security posture. You know how to translate a technical finding into a business decision, and back to the Security department for support. 

  • Experience advising on security for consumer-facing systems, customer data environments, or high-scale operational technology.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and novel technology environments. You have a framework for reasoning under uncertainty and for making recommendations when the answer isn't fully known.

  • M&A or technical due diligence experience is a plus and not required.

The Role

This role is responsible for orchestrating the seamless delivery of dubbing, subtitling, main/episodic titles, accessibility, and marketing assets, ensuring that all localized content reflects Netflix’s creative vision and meets regional standards for quality and authenticity. This role partners closely with internal and external stakeholders, including Content, Post, Marketing, external partners and more, to optimize workflows, resolve operational challenges, and drive continuous improvement. By championing operational excellence, this role plays a critical role in delivering a world-class member experience and supporting the successful global launch of Netflix content.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Localization Ownership

  • Fully own the operational and tactical localization lifecycle for assigned titles, serving as the single point of accountability from kickoff through global launch. 

  • Overseeing all language assets—including dubbing, subtitling, SDH, audio description, marketing supplementals, metadata, main/episodic titles, and forced narratives—proactively managing cross-functional expectations, timelines, budgets, quality control, and ensuring the launch readiness of localized assets for both long form and trailers.

  • Set the tone for the day-to-day partnership between Messaging DSE and CMP, translating open-ended business asks into well-scoped projects, and bringing data-grounded recommendations to inform future strategies

  • Build data solutions that could scale as Messaging innovates and expands into new business verticals (e.g. Live, Games) or channels

  • Exceptional communication skills with technical and non-technical audiences, able to influence your partners using clear actionable insights and recommendations

info.title: Manager, Social Marketing
info.jobDescription:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

This is not just a community manager role.

This is not about posting calendars and managing handles.

This is internet marketing at a cultural scale.
 

We're looking for a cultural operator. A conversation hacker. A genuine content obsessive. Someone who understands the Indian internet deeply, watches everything, and knows how to turn moments into movements. You're as creative as you are analytical — as comfortable pitching a wild idea as you are reading a content slate and knowing exactly which title deserves the internet's attention this week. Loves content coming from different regions in India - Hindi and South. Social at Netflix is a growth engine, an intelligence system, and a brand love machine. If you can balance instinct with insight and culture with craft, this is your playground.
 

The Mandate
 

Build and Lead Conversation

  • Grow and nurture the most engaged OTT community in India.

  • Drive always-on cultural presence beyond Title launches 

  • Ensure Netflix India consistently leads monthly share of voice and shapes how titles travel across press and KOL ecosystems.
     

Turn Social into Strategic Intelligence

  • Mine real-time audience feedback, sentiment, and heat signals.

  • Identify breakout moments early and course-correct underperformance fast.

  • Represent the audience voice in internal forums and influence marketing pivots.

You are both a cultural antenna and a performance radar.

Build Brand Love Through Culture

  • Show up meaningfully across festivals, cultural flashpoints, and everyday usage moments.

  • Create and scale social IP that reinforces Netflix's personality.

  • Work with creators for relevance and credibility, not transactional reach.

  • Bring a programmer's instinct to social — know which stories, scenes, and moments from our slate are worth amplifying, and when, across a title's entire lifecycle.
     

Drive Cross-Functional Impact

  • Work closely with internal teams and marcomms partners to ensure strong ownership on campaigns; align with cross-functional efforts led by Content, Brand, FSM, Publicity, Comms, Product, Partnerships and other teams.

  • Co-own tentpole brand beats across the year.

  • Own reactive excellence and boosting strategy to maximize cultural impact.

Expand Beyond Owned Handles

  • Recognize that the next wave of growth sits beyond metro-heavy legacy communities.

  • Partner with creators, collaborators, and ecosystem players to widen footprint.
     

Who You Are

  • 8 to 10+ years of experience in social marketing, having worked in the entertainment industry, network/studio marketing, global lifestyle / digital-first brands, or a creative agency (experience in the entertainment category preferred).

  • Deep fluency in Indian internet behavior across cohorts and regions.

  • A genuinely creative mind — someone who concepts, not just executes; who pitches ideas that make a room go quiet.

  • Real content programming instincts — you read a slate, know how to sequence conversation around a title's lifecycle, and can spot what's culturally primed to travel before anyone else does.

  • An obsessive, personal love of content — you watch everything, have opinions on everything, and that excitement shows up in the work.

  • Able to balance creative instinct with data-led decision making.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity with high ownership.

  • Strong narrative thinker who understands how social shapes perception.
     

Why This Role Matters
 

At Netflix India, social does not amplify culture. It actively shapes it.

You will influence what trends, what headlines travel, how fandoms form, and how Netflix shows up in everyday conversation across India.
 

If you want to build cultural momentum, not just manage feeds, we would love to hear from you.

The Role

Each Program Manager of Operations is responsible for establishing a structured framework and applying operational rigor to each product domain/subdomain they’re assigned to. As a highly organized and execution-driven contributor, you will partner with cross-functional leaders (from Product, Design, Engineering/TPMs, Data Science & Engineering, etc.) to implement & improve annual planning, quarterly planning, OKR & project tracking, communication, and collaboration. info.jobDescription:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are the JS Applications Platform team. Our mission is to make it fast, safe, and joyful to build and ship the JavaScript software that powers Netflix's enterprise applications — the tools employees and partners use to bring our stories, games, and member experiences to life. The platform we build sits underneath hundreds of applications and services that Netflix depends on to deliver on its mission to entertain the world.

We build the shared foundation that every JavaScript team at Netflix builds on top of; defining the interfaces and building the automations to build and deliver JS software to multiple environments that support the evolving needs of the business. We partner closely with our sibling platform teams to ensure a coherent and consistent platform - so solutions for local dev tooling, CI/CD and others, are built once and reused everywhere rather than being duplicated by multiple teams.

We anchor on the human-facing elements of technology — the judgment, communication, and context that our Culture Memo describes as central to how we work. Code is a small slice of this team's impact.

About This Role

This role is focused on elevating the experience of building and shipping JavaScript software – we want to raise the bar for the daily experience of every JS developer at Netflix. The surface area is broad and includes library and framework development, developer engagement, development tooling, production debugging, operations, and support. 

  • Define and evolve the interfaces (internal CLIs and SDKs) that let each software category — browser, backend, and libraries — integrate with our shared platform

  • Partner closely with the teams building JavaScript software to reimagine the boundaries between the platform and its users — creating cleaner, more independent interfaces that unlock speed and autonomy for everyone

  • Own the core application development platform, along with its CI/CD workflows and supporting services and libraries

  • Lead efforts to make the platform more observable and performant, seeking opportunities to optimize our existing solutions without jeopardizing business critical infrastructure

  • Drive the monorepo and local development experience as shared, cross-category concerns

  • Own infrastructure and deployment integrations that connect our platform to the broader Netflix deployment ecosystem

Excelling In This Role

  • You think in terms of interfaces or contracts, not just implementation — you can look at entangled, load-bearing code and see the clean abstraction trying to get out

  • You've designed and operated CI/CD and release systems at real scale — build pipelines, caching and incremental builds, artifact management, deploy safety — and you've been the person a team leans on when the pipeline breaks.

  • You treat the engineers who build on your platform as customers — you feel their daily friction, sweat the ergonomics of a CLI flag or an error message, and know the difference between tooling that merely works and tooling people reach for by choice.

  • You move work forward across teams you don't sit on — aligning on shared interfaces, negotiating boundaries, and unblocking everyone rather than stalling on whose problem it is — leading with curiosity and humility rather than escalation

  • You design for extensibility, while balancing practicality — addressing immediate needs with solid foundations that can evolve to meet future needs

  • You can balance immediate customer support needs against longer-term work — paying down tech debt and shipping new features — without letting either one consistently crowd out the other

  • You have a record of turning technical ambiguity into clear requirements that empower your team to execute with confidence that they’re building the right thing 

  • You're rigorous about validating changes to shared infrastructure before they ship, and you actively look for ways to move our release processes toward faster, more confident deploys rather than just working around today's gaps

  • You raise the bar for the engineers around you through the patterns and interfaces you set and the design and code feedback you give — you multiply the team without needing to manage it

  • Own end-to-end execution of physical and virtual screenings, including DCP/KDM ingest, subtitle and audio configuration, and onsite or remote technical support.

  • Run the standard technical checklist: venue tech checks before screening day, content re-checks with PSCs before doors open, and standby coverage through the end of the screening, covering AV equipment, projector calibration, audio levels, framing, and safety hazards.

  • Manage day-to-day vendor relationships across the team's 19-vendor active roster spanning DCP creation, QC, tech check/on-site execution, engineering/buildout, and virtual-screening platforms.

  • Keep Glowbot (the team's project-tracking system) current and support ongoing efforts to automate manual admin work.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Publicity, Events, Post Production, and Awards on timing, asset readiness, and market-specific requirements (e.g. classification, versioning).

  • Build and manage vendor relationships across APAC, ensuring reliance on vendors; while helping diversify and strengthen the local vendor bench in each country.

  • Serve as the primary screening project point of contact, navigating language, quality, delivery and stakeholder complexity independently.

Requirements - Must Have

  • Strong project and time management, including composure under reactive, short-notice timelines.

  • Comfortable operating independently in-market; will often be the only Screenings presence in India day to day.

  • Cross-functional collaboration skills: this role sits at the intersection of Publicity, Events, and Post Production and needs to build trust with all three.

  • Stakeholder & Reputation Management: SME support for cross-functional enquiries; filmmaker/executive alignment on sensitive quality conversations.

  • High attention to detail and an excellence bar suited to premiere-level, talent-facing events.

  • Vendor Relationship Management: setting and enforcing service-level expectations with vendors and engineering contractors.

  • Admin: expense tracking, vendor payment system setup, Glowbot access setup.

  • Willing to travel.

Requirements - Preferred

  • Hands-on technical experience in DCI (Digital Cinema Initiatives) and AV: DCP, QC, tech check, and KDM technical understanding, plus real-time pass/fail judgment on site.

  • On-Site Execution: technical producing, day-of-event communication management, on-site vendor accountability.

  • Ability to read and enforce precise digital cinema equipment calibration standards.

  • Business acumen and a "quality gatekeeper" mindset, treating technical execution as a strategic contribution to campaign and awards outcomes, not just delivery.

  • Experience building or managing vendor relationships from scratch in a market, especially valuable given India's current vendor concentration risk.

  • Familiarity with festival or awards-season logistics.

  • Regional Operations: proven ability to manage multi-country logistics independently and adapt to local venue/market conditions.

What Success Looks Like

Screenings run smoothly and on-brand across all APAC markets; vendor relationships are proactively managed and diversified; and cross-functional partners see Screenings as a trusted, strategic partner, not just a technical service.

We are looking for a talented, collaborative and passionate lawyer to join our MACC Legal (Marketing, Ads, Comms and Consumer Products) team in EMEA, dedicated to providing legal support across Netflix’s Marketing, Marketing Partnerships and Advertising Sales teams, across the Nordics region. They must be highly collaborative, working effectively with their MACC legal teammates, internal clients, and cross functional partners, including Title Marketing, Brand Partnerships, Comms, Publicity  Ad Sales, Ads Policy, AdTech, Product, Privacy, and Consumer Products, and Business and Legal Affairs. This is a great opportunity for a mid-level attorney to join our MACC Legal team and support our growing business while continuing to hone their skills and develop their industry knowledge.  

The role will report into the Principal Counsel, MACC, based in Paris. Occasional international travel, including to Paris, and the US, might be required.

  • You are comfortable assessing risk and making smart decisions in the face of ambiguity. 

  • 6-8 years of PQE / legal experience, including direct legal counsel support of publisher, marketing, advertising, brand partnership, media agency, or entertainment/media teams. 

  • You are a qualified lawyer or have a strong legal professional background, highly adept at commercial contracting and negotiating, with very skilled drafting capabilities and a solid grounding in advertising,intellectual property and commercial law across jurisdictions.

  • Approximately 8+ years of experience in advertising sales, agency management, or media partnership roles within Japan’s advertising ecosystem.

info.jobDescription:

AI and ML power innovation in all areas of the business, including helping members choose the right title for them through personalization, better understanding our audience and our content slate, creating high-quality subtitles, dubbings, images, trailers, and other assets, optimizing our payment processing, and much more. AI Platform (AIP) organization builds highly scalable, differentiated AI infrastructure to maximize the business impact of all AI/ML practitioners at Netflix, which is key to accelerating this innovation.

The Opportunity

The AI Observability team makes AI, ML, and Agentic systems transparent, reliable, and production-ready at scale. We build end-to-end observability for ML and GenAI workloads, capturing model inputs, features, predictions, outcomes, and behavior across online and batch systems. Our platform enables teams to monitor model performance, data quality, drift, latency, and failures, turning the ML system from a black box into an explainable, debuggable system. We provide developer-friendly libraries, dashboards, and alerts so teams can debug issues, respond to incidents, and ship AI-powered products with confidence.

We're looking for a hands-on senior engineer to build the frameworks behind Netflix's AI Observability platform, model performance, evaluation, and vendor integration surfaces. You will design reusable infrastructure that enables ML/AI practitioners across domains to monitor model quality in production, evaluate LLM and agentic systems, and adopt vendor tooling through a consistent, self-serve platform. AIP owns the generic, reusable infrastructure; domain teams own their domain-specific evals and remediation. You will partner closely with engineering, product, machine learning, and data teams to turn their needs into reusable platform capabilities. To succeed, you will bring a strong background in AI or ML infrastructure and a passion for building scalable, robust systems.  

In this role, you will:

  • Build the observability framework and platform capabilities that give ML and GenAI systems metrics, logs, and distributed traces across online inference, batch scoring, feature pipelines, and agent orchestration, so teams can instrument their systems consistently.

  • Build the primitives that let teams monitor model performance (accuracy, calibration, error rates), data quality, drift, and degradation on their own systems, rather than monitoring individual models yourself.

  • Build and extend evaluation frameworks for LLM and agentic systems that support response quality, grounding and hallucination, task success, tool-use and trajectory correctness, and LLM-as-a-judge and human-in-the-loop scoring, giving teams reusable building blocks to define and run their own evals.

  • Lead build-vs-buy evaluations for observability and eval tooling, and own the SDKs, connectors, and APIs that integrate vendor platforms into a consistent, well-supported interface, so ML and product teams can onboard models and agents with minimal friction.

  • Build reusable libraries, SDKs, and templates that make observability and evaluation the default for new systems ("observability-by-default"), lowering the barrier for teams to instrument and evaluate their work.

  • Provide the dashboarding, alerting, and SLO/SLI building blocks (plus sensible out-of-the-box templates) that teams use to track model performance, latency, cost, and reliability.

To succeed in this role, you will need:

  • Experience in software, AI/ML, or platform engineering, with hands-on time in production observability, monitoring, or ML/LLM evaluation 

  • Proven track record of designing standards, libraries, SDKs, or frameworks that other teams build on and adopt, reflecting a platform and enablement mindset rather than shipping features for a single use case.

  • Strong coding skills in Python and at least one of Java, Go, or Scala, with experience building production services

  • Practical experience operating ML models in production (online serving and/or batch), including drift, model performance, and data quality.

  • Hands-on experience with modern observability stacks (e.g., Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, ELK/OpenSearch, Jaeger/Tempo, or similar).

  • Solid understanding of distributed systems, microservices, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with ML, data, infra, and product teams, and to communicate clearly about system behavior, quality, and risk.

  • AI-Native Engineering Mindset who uses AI tools as a core part of their own workflow to accelerate design, development, testing, and code review.

Nice to have:

  • Experience building or shipping LLM/GenAI applications and evaluating them: prompt/result logging, evaluation metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, and human-in-the-loop review.

info.jobDescription:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

The Content Localization team, responsible for dubbing, subtitling, accessibility, main/episodic titles, and marketing assets, plays a crucial role in delivering these programs to an expanding international audience by focusing on high-quality localized audio and text services, fostering a collaborative team environment, and utilizing technology.

As a Language Producer, you will ensure that members experience high-quality localized assets, preserving creative intent and enhancing the localized experience for viewers everywhere. With Netflix's global reach and ever-evolving entertainment footprint, localization support for new languages and content genres is essential to our success, making this an exciting time to join the company.

The Role

The Language Producer is the advocate for language quality, creative consistency, and cultural authenticity across all localized Netflix content in their assigned language(s). This role oversees the end-to-end creative and linguistic aspects of dubbing, subtitling, main/episodic titles, accessibility, and marketing assets, serving as the key point of contact for all language-specific localization efforts. Approximately 40% of the role is dedicated to direct title and project coverage—supporting long-form project progress, creative strategy and quality control, and the launch of all localized assets—while the remaining 60% focuses on strategic market and talent development, including workflow innovation, vendor management, and building a robust talent pipeline. This is in support and collaboration with Content Localization Title Producers. The Language Producer partners with internal teams and external talent to deliver high-quality, culturally relevant content. By monitoring language trends and maintaining deep market awareness, this role ensures every Netflix story resonates authentically with local audiences and upholds high standards of creative excellence.

info.jobDescription:

The Role

Behind every title a member streams is a complex content supply chain. Title Launch Management (TLM) is the team that helps design the systems and workflows that bring content, metadata, and rights into Netflix, validate and process them, and orchestrate their path all the way to launch on service. As Netflix expands into new content types and deal structures, this is the team that enables the business to move faster across a growing diversity of partners, formats, and volumes.

We are looking for a strong product leader to serve as Group Product Manager for the TLM Product. You will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap across a portfolio spanning content ingestion pipelines, content distribution and delivery, and the internal platform and tooling that our operations teams rely on every day. Your charter is anchored in three principles: make delivering to Netflix the easiest part of a partner's day, simplify the path between ingestion and publish, and manage risk instead of titles and assets. 

Your team of Product Managers partners with Engineering, Operations, and Design to build and scale the platforms, services, and tools that move content through the business — while resisting the temptation to treat every new deal as a bespoke one-off. Just as importantly, you will be a close product partner to the operational teams who run these workflows, turning their hardest problems into a durable product strategy. This is a high-leverage role with direct impact on the speed, quality, and cost with which content reaches members around the world.

In this role, you will:

  • Set the strategy: define and drive the multi-quarter product vision for TLM, connecting ingestion, distribution, and platform investments to measurable reductions in manual intervention and turnaround time across content archetypes.

  • Own the products that make delivering to Netflix effortless: unified direct delivery via APIs, web portals, and standards-based feeds; spec-agnostic ingestion; partner onboarding and permissioning; metadata capture; and automated asset evaluation and QC.

  • Lead distribution & the path to publish: own the orchestration that simplifies the path between ingestion and launch — automation as the default launch path, an extensible catalog architecture that lets new content bets evolve safely, and reliable fulfillment to the platforms and systems the business depends on.

  • Partner with operations and key cross-functional team: act as the primary product partner to operational teams; translate operational pain points into a prioritized backlog and pair operational KPIs (turnaround time, launch readiness, issues per launch, manual steps reduced) with product investment. Work with partner domains to streamline asset workflows and launches.

  • Lead and grow a team: hire, coach, and develop a team of Product Managers; set clear goals, raise the bar on product craft, and create the conditions for your PMs to do the best work of their careers.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment: partner across Rights, Encoding Technologies, Localization, Content Foundations, Member Product, and Operations to sequence dependencies, drive effective debate, and land crisp decisions.

  • Communicate with clarity: use top-notch written and verbal communication to provide context to stakeholders ranging from individual engineers to senior leadership, and to uncover new areas of opportunity.

Your Background Includes:

  • 10+ years of product management experience for b2b focused products

  • A track record shipping complex technical or platform products ideally in content supply chain, media processing, ingestion/distribution pipelines, workflow orchestration, developer/partner platforms, or large-scale operational systems.

  • Strong systems thinking and technical acumen: comfort reasoning about pipelines, APIs, data models, automation, and the trade-offs between speed, quality, cost, and risk. You don't need to code, but you should work deeply with engineering.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner with operational teams and translate operational realities into product strategy and roadmap.

  • Data-driven analysis and decision-making, with excellent judgment and prioritization in ambiguous, high-scale environments.

  • Experience building automation- or ML/AI-powered products that reduce manual effort at scale is a strong plus.

  • Demonstrated experience collaborating across engineers, designers, data scientists, and business partners in a highly cross-functional, matrixed organization.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication, including the ability to present technical content to non-technical audiences.

  • People leadership with experience developing talent, giving candid feedback, and elevating the craft of the PMs around them.

  • Experience in media, entertainment, or streaming is a strong plus.

What We Offer

  • Meaningful impact. The systems you own are foundational to how hundreds of millions of members experience Netflix — and to how efficiently the business operates.

  • Responsibility. Netflix offers true transparency and autonomy. Our culture is unique and is key to how we innovate.

  • Stunning colleagues. You'll work with high-performing peers across product, engineering, and operations who value collaboration and from whom you can learn.

info.title: Lead UX Designer - Games
info.jobDescription:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

Who We Are

From games on TV to mobile and web, Next Games is a Netflix first-party studio that develops approachable games to entertain a diverse, global audience. 

We design games that Netflix members can enjoy every day as part of their subscription. Our games released on Netflix to date include TV games Boggle Party, Pictionary Game Night, Party Crashers: Fool Your Friends, and Underwatermelon, as well as Netflix Puzzled, available on mobile devices and on tudum.com.  

We proudly combine our Finnish game development culture with Netflix's global entertainment culture, embracing the strengths of both and empowering our talented and diverse teams to deliver their best work yet. 

The Role

As a Lead UX Designer, you will help create high-quality games that are playable, enjoyable, and accessible to a broad audience. In this role, you will work closely with your team daily and develop and execute a strategic UX vision for each of our games, demonstrating a deep understanding of our audience and their needs as players.

You will maintain consistent relationships with players and provide valuable insights to the team, enabling a player-centric approach to improving game features and iterations. Your excellent communication skills and strong sense of teamwork make you a supportive collaborator. You are passionate about accessibility, with years of experience advocating for best practices and championing inclusive design. As the studio’s accessibility expert, you will lead accessibility efforts, mentor your team, and ensure our games are welcoming to all players.

Responsibilities

  • Guide the team through all steps of the UX process to holistically improve the game experience.

  • Design accessible, usable, and enjoyable UX for a broad, casual audience, defining game communication, structure, and content strategy.

  • Champion accessibility as the studio expert: lead best practices, facilitate workshops, and ensure guidelines are current and implemented.

  • Manage, mentor, and support team members, fostering growth in UX and accessibility.

  • Apply scientific methods and Design Thinking to UX research, testing, and feature development, ensuring data-driven decisions.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (UX researchers, UI artists, designers, artists, leads, stakeholders) to enhance processes and game quality.

  • Advocate for players through direct community engagement and sharing insights to inform design.

  • Develop and maintain frameworks for heuristic evaluation and share clear, polished documentation.

Skills and Abilities

  • Proven experience designing for both web and app platforms, taking features from concept through implementation.

  • Expertise in accessibility and inclusive design, including running accessibility tests and leading workshops.

  • Strong foundation in scientific UX research methods, including hypothesis testing, experimental design, and data analysis.

  • Ability to design game architecture, flows, wireframes, and interactive prototypes (Figma).

  • Experience with user research tools (e.g., PlaytestCloud) and basic Unity skills.

  • Excellent visual design, communication, leadership, and mentoring abilities.

  • Commitment to player-centric, collaborative, and iterative development.

  • Skilled in creating and maintaining thorough documentation and advancing UX maturity within the team.

The Team

You’ll join a diverse studio environment, working primarily from our Helsinki office. We value transparent communication, proactive problem-solving, and enthusiasm for crafting accessible experiences. As the Lead UX Designer, you will play a key role in shaping the future of our player experiences at Next Games.

You'll gain exposure to every stage of the production lifecycle while helping ensure our productions are financially sound, operationally efficient, and positioned for success.

What You'll Do

Partner with Productions

  • Work closely with production companies, line producers, production accountants, production auditors and internal Netflix teams throughout the lifecycle of a production.

  • Build trusted relationships with creative, production, legal, business affairs, tax, accounts payable, and external stakeholders to ensure smooth financial operations.

  • Support production partners by providing guidance on Netflix's financial policies, reporting expectations, and production finance processes.

Drive Financial Excellence

  • Review and analyze production budgets, cost reports, cash flows, and forecasts.

  • Monitor production spend against approved budgets and identify financial risks, trends, and opportunities early.

  • Partner with productions to develop accurate Estimates to Complete (ETCs) and final cost projections.

  • Perform variance analysis and communicate meaningful insights that support business decisions.

  • Review invoices, funding requests, and production payments for accuracy and compliance.

Deliver Meaningful Insights

  • Go beyond validating numbers by identifying cost optimization opportunities and operational efficiencies.

  • Analyze production schedules, resource utilization, and spending patterns to proactively highlight financial risks and recommendations.

  • Prepare concise financial summaries and presentations for internal stakeholders to support investment decisions.

Strengthen Financial Operations

  • Map production costs to Netflix's Chart of Accounts and maintain accurate financial records.

  • Update production data across Netflix's internal systems and reporting tools.

  • Partner with auditors and production accountants to ensure timely, accurate, and compliant financial reporting.

  • Help improve reporting processes, financial controls, and operational efficiencies across productions.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with people just as much as they enjoy working with numbers. You are someone who is naturally curious, asks thoughtful questions, and isn't satisfied with simply reconciling numbers—you want to understand the story behind them.

You'll be successful in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in Production Finance, Production Accounting, Production Management, or a similar role within the film, television, or media industry.

  • Strong understanding of production budgeting, cost reporting, forecasting, and production accounting.

  • Experience working with production companies, studios, line producers, or production accountants.

  • Excellent financial analysis and problem-solving skills with strong business judgment.

  • Advanced Excel skills and proficiency in Google Workspace; experience with production accounting software is an advantage.

  • Working knowledge of Tally or similar accounting systems is preferred.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across multiple teams.

  • Exceptional attention to detail while maintaining the ability to see the bigger picture.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Commerce, or a related discipline. CA or equivalent professional qualification is preferred.

Who You Are

  • You thrive in fast-moving environments and enjoy solving new challenges every day.

  • You are proactive, resourceful, and comfortable navigating ambiguity.

  • You build strong relationships and enjoy partnering with diverse teams.

  • You balance analytical thinking with practical decision-making.

  • You have high standards, strong integrity, and a commitment to excellence.

  • You're passionate about entertainment and excited to help bring incredible stories to audiences around the world.

Why Netflix?

At Netflix, you'll have the opportunity to work on some of the most exciting productions in the industry while partnering with exceptionally talented people across creative, production, and business teams.

You'll be trusted with meaningful responsibility from day one, encouraged to challenge conventional thinking, and empowered to make an impact on how world-class stories are produced.

If you're excited by the idea of combining finance, strategy, and storytelling, we'd love to hear from you.

info.title: Engineering Manager, Ads Signals & Targeting
info.jobDescription:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Since launching our ad-supported tier in 2022, the momentum has been unstoppable—we reach over 94 million global monthly active users! As we enter our fourth year, our ambition is massive, and we are just getting started.

Our Team

The Ads Engineering team at Netflix is dedicated to creating a world-class advertising ecosystem that drives our advertising business. This team's mission is to develop advanced technology that ensures exceptional experiences for both our members and advertisers. Our responsibilities encompass a broad spectrum of products, ranging from sales and media planning to optimizing advertiser outcomes and execution. This includes inventory and order management, campaign execution, ad serving, audience and identity management, measurement, reporting, and finance.

We use several Netflix investments and innovations - a unique mix of client and server-side ad insertions, state-of-the-art content delivery systems, ad encoding recipes, content understanding, and metadata, etc. We deliver ads in a manner that’s thoughtful of our member’s viewing experience and drive great outcomes for advertisers. We also ensure that advertiser brand safety is ensured during serving so that members only see the most appropriate ads for them.

Our team is faced with the enormous ambitions of building highly performant advertising systems and delivering high impact to our business by monetizing our incredible slate of content. As one of the newest entrants in the Connected TV advertising space that’s rapidly growing, we seek to build unique value propositions that help us differentiate us and become a market leader in record time. Our roles come with expectations of delivering in a rapid clip,  comfort with  lofty goals and big ambitions,   the visibility that comes with strategic initiatives, and  responsibility and an appetite to operate like a startup within an established company.

We are looking for a highly motivated engineering leader to drive the evolution of our core targeting and signals platforms for Netflix Ads. This team builds and scales the foundational systems behind audience and contextual targeting, enabling more relevant, privacy-forward ad experiences for our members and better performance for our advertisers. By connecting the right message to the right moment, Ads Core Targeting helps create an experience that feels personalized, valuable, and consistent with the quality members expect from Netflix.

As an Engineering Manager you will:

  • Own the core signals and targeting systems that power relevant ads for Netflix members.

  • Start from a solid foundation, with significant room to evolve the platform.

  • Partner closely with ML teams to build advanced interest, lookalike, and expansion models.

  • Work on high-scale, low-latency services that enrich every ad request in real time.

  • Shape how Netflix activates first‑party and partner signals for targeting, optimization, and measurement.

  • Drive success in a fast paced, flat organization with minimal process and a heavy emphasis on ownership.

  • Support your team by contextualizing the larger vision, enabling prioritization and fostering high focus and executional excellence.

  • Operate as an ambassador of the Netflix Culture

  • Create a dream team by hiring, retaining, and growing high performing talent.

Skills & experience we’re seeking:

  • Proven experience leading teams that build and operate high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems in  ads targeting, or similarly demanding domains

  • Hands-on background with signal services for ad request enrichment, including real‑time and batch data integration

  • Strong familiarity with contextual and profile-based signals and how they are used for audience and contextual targeting

  • Experience designing and managing signals registration, governance, and curation frameworks

  • Expertise with targeting and audience definition metadata (e.g., taxonomies, hierarchies, schemas, configuration management)

  • Experience leading ML engineers building and operating modeled profile audiences and lookalike models, including taking these models from development through integration into production systems.

  • Track record of building and leading high-performing engineering teams, setting technical direction, and delivering complex platform initiatives

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and define clear strategies in a fast-evolving ads landscape

  • Excellent communication skills; you can explain complex systems to both technical and non-technical partners

  • 10+ years of total experience with 3+ years of management experience in building and leading diverse software engineering teams. 

  • A strong product mindset along with experience in delivering large complex projects collaborating with a variety of cross-functional stakeholders that are technology, operations or business focused.

  • General understanding of the advertising marketplace and landscape. 

  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking with demonstrated product sense and leadership in the working environment

Nice to haves:

  • Familiarity with legal compliance and changing landscape of ads regulations around the world.

  • Familiarity with ML and advertising systems that leverage data to drive optimal outcomes for the users and the business.

  • Experience working in the CTV space and knowledge of its unique constraints

info.jobDescription:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. About The Team

The Live Ad Insertions team sits at the intersection of broadcast engineering, streaming infrastructure, and digital advertising. Our mission is to deliver a seamless, high-reliability ad insertion experience across live and linear streams, from primetime tentpole events like the NFL and live sports to 24/7 linear feeds and breaking news. We own the full stack of tools, systems, and operational infrastructure required to trigger, stitch, monitor, and verify ad breaks in real time at scale, without compromising the member experience.

Live advertising is one of the highest-stakes, highest-reward surfaces in CTV. When tens of millions of concurrent viewers are watching a single event, there are no second chances. A break happens once, in real time, and the window to act is measured in seconds. That demands more than reliable systems: it demands proactive observability tooling that can detect anomalies before they surface to members, and the ability to make real-time corrections mid-event when something does go wrong. This team operates with the precision of a broadcast NOC and the velocity of a software startup. We are responsible for the technology that turns a live signal into a monetized ad experience, at scale, millisecond by millisecond.

As an Engineering Manager, You Will

Lead a team of engineers building the real-time infrastructure, tooling, and operational systems for live ad insertion across server-side, client-side, and server-guided delivery models.

  • Own the reliability and operational excellence of ad insertion during 24/7 linear streams and high-stakes live events, including NFL games, live sports, and awards shows.

  • Define the technical roadmap for live ad insertion, including SCTE signal ingestion and validation, ad pod management, manifest stitching, slate handling, and ad decisioning integration.

  • Partner with ad operations, broadcast engineering, content delivery, and ad serving teams to ensure seamless signal-to-slot execution from ingest to client playback.

  • Drive hiring, retention, and development of a high-performing engineering team capable of operating in a demanding live environment.

  • Establish the on-call and incident response culture for live ad systems, setting SLAs and runbooks for break-glass scenarios during high-profile live events.

  • Contextualize your team's larger advertising strategy and translate business priorities into a technically sound, executable plan.

  • Serve as the technical authority in cross-functional discussions on live ad capabilities, representing the team to leadership, partners, and vendors.

Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • 10+ years of total engineering experience with 3+ years managing software engineering teams in a live media, streaming, or ad tech context.

  • Effective communicator across both technical and business stakeholders, including ad sales, ad operations, broadcast engineering, and executive leadership.

  • Strong track record of hiring and developing senior engineers in competitive talent markets.

  • Ability to operate in a flat, fast-moving organization, balancing long-term architectural investments against immediate operational needs.

  • Proven track record of engineering for high-availability, zero-downtime live events, including building operational tooling for ad ops (e.g., real-time fill rate tracking, signal health visualization, and break monitoring workflows).

  • Strong understanding of ad servers, DSPs, and VAST 4.x/VMAP in live contexts, with a focus on managing strict decisioning latency budgets, timeout handling, tracking event firing, and mitigating the cascading effects of decision failures.

Nice to Haves

  • Vendor Relationships: Experience collaborating with content and distribution partners, including MVPDs, vMVPDs, and broadcast networks, on joint live ad insertion implementations.

  • Streaming Pipelines & Architecture: Deep hands-on experience with live streaming pipelines (from ingest protocols like RTMP, SRT, or TS through to CDN) and ad insertion architectures, including SSAI, CSAI, and SGAI (HLS interstitials/DASH).

  • Broadcast Standards & Splicing: Expertise in broadcast signaling (SCTE-35, SCTE-104, SCTE-224) and manifest manipulation for ad stitching, alongside familiarity with master control and linear playout systems.

  • Ad Pod Construction & Encoding: Advanced knowledge of managing live break constraints, including slate/fallback handling, break reconciliation, and encoding constraints (codec/bitrate matching, frame rate alignment) to prevent playback artifacts.

Our work focuses on the core platform architectures supporting ranking and scoring, auction mechanics, budget and pacing systems, and goal-based delivery optimization. What You'll Do

  • Operational Excellence & Resiliency:  Architect a system that is straightforward to operate and maintain. Maintain a high standard for distributed systems design and resiliency, ensuring graceful degradation during traffic spikes or live events.

  • Concurrency & Algorithmic Design: Practical experience with multi-threaded systems design, concurrent programming, and algorithmic design for highly concurrent workloads (including lock-free data structures or lock contention mitigation).

info.title: Coordinator, Content - Netflix Animation Studios
info.jobDescription:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

The Netflix Animation Studios Content Team is looking for a proactive and creatively driven Content Coordinator for the Original Animated Features Content team. In this role, you will serve as a critical organizational force while also providing deep creative support for our diverse slate of feature films. You will be at the heart of the development and production process, collaborating closely with our executives, filmmakers, and cross-functional teams to bring our stories to life.

About The Team:

The Animated Film Content team is driving much of the creative inception at the studio, responsible for steering the development of our animated film slate. This visionary team collaborates with writers, directors, and artists to nurture fresh ideas and transform them into captivating films. By overseeing the creative process from concept to completion, they ensure each project aligns with our studio's vision and resonates with audiences worldwide. With a keen eye for storytelling and innovation, the Animated Film Content team crafts narratives that are not only entertaining but also deeply engaging, cementing our studio's reputation for excellence in animation.

What You’ll Do:

Creative Strategy & Show Support

  • Creative Evaluation & Coverage: Review incoming creative materials (scripts, outlines, bibles, storyboards) and provide timely, actionable, and thoughtful coverage for executives.

  • Strategic Partnership: Support the Lead Executive by taking detailed notes during show meetings, driving meeting preparation, setting agendas, and ensuring review documents are finalized ahead of critical check-ins.

  • Development Research: Conduct deep-dive creative research on key titles during the early development phase, and provide Netflix-facing support for filmmaker research trips (including finance and security coordination).

  • Production Logistics: Support critical milestone tracking, anticipate a show’s pivotal moments, and draft initial passes at critical show documentation (e.g., greenlight and pivot memos).

Talent Discovery & Industry Networking

  • Talent Sourcing: Support targeted writer and talent searches based on executive needs. This includes soliciting samples, curating and assembling batches, checking availabilities, and facilitating filmmaker meetings.

  • Industry Engagement: Cultivate and maintain active relationships with covering agents, managers, and industry peers to consistently source top-tier writing and directing samples.

  • Creator Meetings: Participate in general meetings with emerging filmmakers and join executives in high-level pitches to help evaluate incoming material.

Operations & Cross-Functional Support

  • Cross-Functional Point-of-Contact: Serve as a primary liaison connecting filmmakers with critical cross-functional departments (Production, Business & Legal Affairs, Marketing, Consumer Products, PR), providing resources and keeping partners aligned on the latest show status.

  • Deal & Onboarding Execution: Assist with the seamless onboarding of key Above-the-Line (ATL) creative hires (Directors, Writers, Creative Producers) into the Netflix ecosystem. Trigger payments for creative deliverables in partnership with BALA, maintaining internal applications for deal creation and tracking.

  • Information Architecture: Maintain and optimize internal trackers, apps, and drives to ensure seamless information sharing. Continuously identify and implement efficiencies in file management, communication channels, and overall team operations.

  • Submission Management: Field incoming pitches, meticulously log submissions, and coordinate coverage on writing and visual development samples.

What You’ll Need:

  • Experience: 3+ years of robust industry work experience, ideally within a studio, network, production company, agency, or management firm (prior experience as a Coordinator, Executive Assistant, or Production Supervisor preferred).

  • Pipeline Literacy: Deep, direct familiarity with the feature animation workflow (Story, Visual Development, Editorial, Post) and studio production pipelines.

  • Industry Acumen: Proven experience and high comfort level collaborating with top-level internal and external talent, filmmakers, and senior executives.

  • Business & Operational Acumen: Strong organizational discipline with a baseline understanding of Above-The-Line deal structures, talent representation, and cross-functional studio operations.

  • Passion: A deep, demonstrable passion for Animated Features and/or Kids & Family Content. You should be an avid consumer of animation with strong opinions on storytelling and the current landscape.

  • Communication: Excellent communication and professional writing skills, with the ability to distill complex creative discussions into clear, actionable notes and executive memos.

  • Agility & Autonomy: A self-starter who takes initiative, anticipates bottlenecks, and effectively multitasks within a fast-paced, high-volume environment with minimal supervision.

Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:


We are seeking a Head of Character Effects (CFX) to support our upcoming animated feature film. The Head of Character Effects works inside of NAS as the show-based leader for all character-related secondary motion, including hair, fur, feathers, cloth, and garments. They will partner closely with the Director, Production Designer, VFX Supervisor, Art Director, Head of Characters, Head of Character Animation and Technical Supervisor to ensure that character effects are both artistically compelling and technically robust.

The Head of Character Effects will oversee the CFX team during asset development, look development, and shot production. They will define the simulation approach for the show, review and give notes on all CFX work, and ensure it meets the highest quality bar while remaining efficient and stable in production. This may involve developing or supervising prototypes, guiding grooming and garment construction for simulation, solving complex technical problems, and helping to set up the CFX side of the project for success.

This position is essential in bridging the gap between creative intent and simulation-driven workflows, ensuring that character motion feels alive, expressive, and fully aligned with the film’s visual language. The Head of Character Effects builds strong relationships with creative leadership and with technical and production partners, demonstrating great diplomatic and interpersonal skills to balance artistic ambition with schedule and pipeline constraints.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and supervise Character Effects across the show, from look development to final shot delivery

  • Define the creative and technical approach for hair, fur, cloth, feathers, and other character-related simulations

  • Review CFX assets and shots, providing clear, actionable artistic and technical notes

  • Collaborate with Directors, Production Designers, Art Directors, Head of Characters, Animation, FX, and Look Development to ensure CFX supports character performance and story

  • Partner with Technical Supervisors, Production Technology, and R&D to develop and maintain robust, efficient CFX tools and workflows

  • Anticipate and identify creative and technical challenges in CFX and offer practical, innovative solutions

  • Work with Production Management on bids, schedules, and priorities to deliver high-quality work on time and within scope

  • Mentor and support CFX Supervisors, Leads, and Artists, fostering growth, clarity, and a positive team culture

  • Communicate effectively across disciplines, translating complex technical concepts into accessible language for creative partners

  • Collaborate with grace, humility, inclusion, and open-mindedness

What You’ll Need:

  • At least 10 years of experience in Character Effects/FX within film, TV, or games, including 5–7 years in leadership or supervisory roles on large-scale animated features or VFX films

  • Proven, production-level expertise in Houdini (SOPs/DOPs/POPs), with strong understanding of cloth, hair, fur, feather, and soft-body simulations; muscle/skin experience is a plus

  • Strong scripting and/or programming skills (e.g., Python, VEX) and familiarity with Linux-based workflows

  • Deep understanding of the end-to-end 3D animation pipeline and how CFX interacts with Modeling, Grooming, Rigging, Surfacing, Animation, FX, Lighting, and Compositing

  • A strong eye for movement, weight, and anatomy, and the ability to give clear, constructive notes that improve performance and appeal

  • Excellent leadership, communication, and mentoring skills, with the ability to build trust and enthusiasm across a cross-site team while fostering a respectful, collaborative, and inclusive environment.

  • Comfort balancing quick turnaround needs with long-term quality and technical stability


 

This role is based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Hybrid Role (Minimum of 3 days a week in the office). 

At NAS, we carefully consider a wide range of compensation factors to determine your compensation. We rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, location, skills, and experience. The overall market range for this role is typically $205k -$259k CAD. This reflects total compensation; we do not have stock options.

NAS benefits can include medical/dental/vision plans, mental health support, retirement programs, and family-forming benefits, paid leave of absence programs, and paid time away programs to be used for vacation and sick paid time off. See more detail about our benefits here.

info.jobDescription:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:

The Head of Environments works inside of NAS as the show-based leader for all digital environments, sets, and props. They will partner closely with the Director, Production Designer, VFX Supervisor, Art Director (Environments), Head of Assets, and Technical Supervisor to ensure that environmental designs are both artistically compelling and technically robust.

The Head of Environments will oversee the environment asset teams—including Modeling, Surfacing, and Matte Painting—during asset development, look development, and shot production. They will define the technical and artistic approach for environment construction, review and give notes on all set and prop builds, and ensure they meet the highest quality bar while remaining efficient and stable in production. This involves translating 2D concepts into 3D space, guiding camera projections and matte painting integration, solving complex technical pipeline challenges, and helping set up the environmental asset build of the project for success.

This position is essential in bridging the gap between artistic vision and 3D technical reality, ensuring that digital environments feel immersive, stylized, and fully aligned with the film’s visual language. The Head of Environments builds strong relationships with creative leadership and technical/production partners, demonstrating great leadership and communication skills to balance artistic ambition with schedule, budget, and pipeline constraints.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and supervise environment asset creation across the show, providing creative and technical guidance for digital environments, sets, and props.

  • Define the creative and technical approach for modeling, surfacing, camera projections, and matte painting elements in line with the Director's vision.

  • Drive team reviews and provide detailed, actionable creative and technical feedback to Modeling, Surfacing, and DMP departments.

  • Collaborate with Directors, Production Designers, Art Directors, and VFX Supervisors to effectively translate 2D environment designs into 3D production-ready sets.

  • Partner with Technical Supervisors, Production Technology, and pipeline teams to define, optimize, and maintain efficient asset-creation tools and standardized canonical workflows.

  • Mentor and support Modeling, Surfacing, and DMP Supervisors and artists, fostering professional growth, skill development, and a positive team culture.

  • Communicate effectively across disciplines, translating complex technical concepts into accessible language for creative partners and vice versa.

  • Collaborate with grace, humility, inclusion, and open-mindedness.

What You’ll Need

  • At least 10 years of experience in environment asset creation within film, TV, or games, including 5–7 years in a leadership or supervisory role on large-scale animated features or VFX films.

  • Expert knowledge of Modeling and Surfacing workflows, with a deep understanding of 3D environment layout, asset builds, volume, form, and camera projections.

  • Proven production-level proficiency in Maya and ZBrush/Mudbox, texturing packages (Substance, Mari, Photoshop), and matte painting/projection workflows.

  • Expert understanding of digital film pipelines and related technologies, including Katana, RenderMan, and real-time pipelines.

  • Strong 2D skills to quickly mock up and iterate concepts, helping define the visual and spatial rules of the environments.

  • Experience with project management and production tracking systems such as Flow Production Tracking (ShotGrid).

  • Excellent leadership, communication, and mentoring skills, with the ability to foster collaboration across diverse departments and personalities.

info.title: Lighting Supervisor
info.jobDescription:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:
We are seeking a Lighting Supervisor to support our upcoming animated feature film. The Lighting Supervisor works inside of NAS to lead the lighting team on a specific film or series, overseeing the lighting of shots and sequences to realize the cinematic vision of the show. This role ensures that lighting supports the story, mood, and visual style, and that lit shots are technically robust and ready for compositing and final delivery.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and mentor a team of lighting artists, casting work appropriately and providing clear, constructive feedback in dailies and reviews

  • Collaborate with the VFX Supervisor, Head of Cinematography, Lighting, Production Designer, and Art Directors to establish the lighting style, color palette, and quality bar for the show

  • Supervise the lighting of shots and sequences, ensuring that lighting choices support story, performance, and visual continuity

  • Create or refine selected key lighting shots or setups as needed—particularly complex, hero, or reference‑setting work—to help establish the quality bar, style, and technical approach for the team

  • Work closely with Surfacing, FX, CFX, Matte Painting, and Compositing teams to ensure assets and renders are prepared and integrated efficiently into the lighting workflow

  • Help define and refine lighting tools, rigs, templates, and workflows in partnership with Technical Supervisors, TDs, and pipeline teams

  • Provide input to Production Management and department leadership on lighting complexity and progress to support realistic planning and prioritization

  • Troubleshoot technical and artistic challenges in lighting, collaborating on solutions that maintain quality while meeting schedule needs

  • Help foster a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative team culture where artists can do their best work

What You’ll Need:

  • Significant experience as a Lighting Artist in feature animation, VFX, or high‑end series, including time in a Lead or Supervisory role

  • A strong reel demonstrating high-quality lighting and rendering, with a deep understanding of color, mood, and cinematic storytelling

  • Proficiency with industry-standard lighting and rendering tools (e.g., Maya, Katana, Houdini, and renderers such as Arnold, RenderMan, or similar)

  • Strong understanding of how lighting interacts with Modeling, Surfacing, FX, CFX, Matte Painting, Compositing, and Rendering within a production pipeline

  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to give clear, constructive feedback and collaborate effectively across departments

  • Strong organizational and problem‑solving skills

This role is based out of Sydney, Australia. Hybrid Role (Minimum of 3 days a week in the office).

info.title: Technical Trainer - Netflix Animation Studios
info.jobDescription:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

The Talent Development and Training team aims to centralize and streamline training to ensure an equitable and consistent learning experience across all production departments. By fostering a culture of learning and development, we believe it is essential to create training programs that equip individuals at all levels with the skills and tools needed to collaborate effectively, lead teams, drive innovation, and uphold our high standards of creative excellence.

Job Summary:

Netflix Animation is looking for a Technical Trainer to join our global, end-to-end feature studio. As a Training Specialist, you will manage a diverse set of responsibilities aimed at advancing technical and enrichment education. Your contributions will include designing and organizing curriculum, leading training sessions on industry-standard and proprietary Netflix Animation tools, and developing and maintaining training content for tools and workflows across the production pipeline.

The Technical Trainer will be a key member of a global team, reporting directly to the Director of Production Training and Talent Development. In this collaborative role, they will work alongside the Technical Trainer in Vancouver and partner with various cross-functional teams to develop educational content and courses that address the evolving needs of artists and production teams across Netflix Animation Studios.


What You’ll Do:

  • Onboarding/New Hire Training: Support the design and delivery of Netflix Animation's new-hire onboarding curriculum by providing a best-in-class new-hire training experience.

  • Department Training Support: Partner with subject-matter experts to deliver training on fundamental skills (e.g., cinematography, design), technical tools (e.g., Maya, Houdini, Nuke), and studio practices (e.g., pipelines and workflows).

  • Custom Course Creation: As needed, partner with tech and production departments to leverage internal training assets, develop course outlines, and support the transformation of existing materials into courses and workshops.

  • SME Course Support: Support subject matter experts in developing course outlines, learning objectives, and instructional design.

  • LMS Management: Support the Learning Management System by creating, uploading, and tracking courses and Instructor-Led Trainings (ILTs).  This can also include designing icons, buttons, and graphics for LMS and Courses.

  • Training Material Maintenance: Maintain and update existing training materials to align with production workflows. Create new materials tailored to the team or studio-wide.

  • Collaboration and Instruction: Collaborate with grace, humility, inclusion, and an open mind. Work with Artist Management, Production, and Technology teams to understand training needs and deliver intermediate and advanced technical training solutions.

  • Training & Event Support: Maintain training spaces (rooms, classrooms, equipment, and software), coordinate with Tech/AV, manage scheduling with the Training Coordinator, and help organize and deliver internal and cross-studio learning events.

  • Team Collaboration: Partner with productions, department leadership, and Artist Management to identify training opportunities to help support craft department workshops. 

What You’ll Need:

  • Teaching and Instructional Design: Expertise in designing and delivering engaging training sessions, both in-person and online, with a passion for teaching. Skilled in instructional design and using assessment tools to measure effectiveness.

  • Technical and Industry Expertise: Possess a deep understanding and first-hand working knowledge of CG production pipelines and team collaboration in film production. Proficient in 3D animation tooling such as Maya, Mari, Houdini (including Solaris), and Nuke, as well as navigating complex proprietary tools and production workflows, utilizing USD.

  • Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences, demonstrating strong verbal, written, and interpersonal skills. Experience working in a global team environment. Capable of building and maintaining strong team relationships, appreciating cultural and business nuances globally.

  • Problem-Solving and Adaptability: Proven experience in diagnosing and resolving technical issues in a fast-paced environment. Skilled in maintaining composure under pressure and adept at thriving in a rapidly growing, global studio environment. Must be capable of supporting constant change and managing ambiguity effectively.

  • Organizational and Documentation Skills: Strong organizational and time-management abilities, with experience in documentation using platforms like Confluence and Google Workspace

  • Curiosity and Partnership Approach: Demonstrate strong curiosity and an advisory approach in understanding and translating talent needs into training initiatives and programming, with a proven track record of at least two successful program implementations.

  • Background / Experience: Blended experience in Film Production, Feature Animation, or a related field, together with a background in educational learning and development or an equivalent role.  Strong understanding of the feature animation production pipeline and related tools (e.g., Houdini, Maya).

This role is based in Sydney, Australia. Hybrid Role (Minimum requirement of 3 days a week in the office).

info.title: Sr. Account Manager (Germany) - 14 Month Fixed Term Contract
info.jobDescription:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

This is a 14-month fixed-term contract role, based in either Berlin office 3 days per week, or remotely from Hamburg or Munich.
 

The Senior Account Manager will be responsible for leading the pre-to-post sale campaign execution workflow as a strategic partner to Netflix Sales Partner(s) in Germany.
